newsitem.title: USA: NYC Oct tax revenues flat, still expects surplus.
newsitem.headline: NYC Oct tax revenues flat, still expects surplus.

text.p: New York City tax revenue collections were flat in October, but the city is still on track for a $450 million revenue surplus for fiscal year 1997, city officials said Thursday at City Hall.

In addition, the city said its fiscal year projected budget gaps for 1998, 1999 and 2000 were reduced, city budget director Joseph Lhota told reporters at a news conference. The fiscal year begins July 1.

Lhota, releasing the city first quarter modification for the FY 1997 budget, said, "I think the number $450 million achieving this, however, depends on how well Wall Street performs the rest of the fiscal year. Lhota attributed the projected tax revenue surplus in part to Wall Street's recovery.
The city projected that the budget gap in FY 1998 will fall to $1.23 billion from $1.7 billion, partly due to the proposed $400 million in city agency spending cuts.
In the out years, for fiscal year 1999, the gap is projected at about $2.3 billion, down from almost $2.7 billion, with $950 million of agency spending cuts included.
For fiscal 2000, the gap is projected to be jsut over $3 billion, down from $3.4 billion. The city expects to cut agency spending by $1.35 billion in that year.
